Some Walgreens locations still have free public blood pressure machines near their pharmacy waiting areas, but availability varies significantly. Many stores removed or unplugged them during the COVID-19 pandemic, and others have phased them out entirely.

- **Availability:** Hit or miss. You must call your local Walgreens store ahead of time to confirm if a working public machine is still on-site.

- **Accuracy:** Public kiosk machines can drift out of calibration and may provide less reliable readings than a properly fitted personal cuff.

### Home Blood Pressure Monitors

If your local store does not have a public machine or you prefer reliable tracking, Walgreens stocks a large selection of automatic upper-arm and wrist monitors for purchase

: [](https://www.walgreens.com/store/c/blood-pressure-monitors/ID=361299-tier3)

- **Walgreens Brand Auto Arm Monitor:** ~$30 to $50

- **Omron Upper Arm Series (3, 7, or 10 Series):** ~$45 to $95

- **Wrist Monitors:** ~$35 to $50 [](https://www.walgreens.com/q/blood+pressure+monitors)
